newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek equities give ground, unmoved by reform talk.
newsitem.headline: Greek equities give ground, unmoved by reform talk.

text.p: Greek equities failed to follow up on Wednesday's mild rebound and traded lower in moderate turnover boosted by block trades, nonchalant to reform talk by bourse authorities.

"The market didn't look enthused by the reform talk. Fundamentally, it is cheap but demand is presently weak, the product doesn't seem to sell well. November historically has not been a good month for Greek shares. Chances of the market taking off look slim right now," said portfolio manager Dimitris Katsabekis at Agricultural Bank Mutual Funds.
"Technically, the market gave sell signals on October 10 and it is trending toward support at 880-900, this is where it is headed," he said.
The Athens general share index closed down 0.53 percent, or 4.85 points lower at 915.49 from Wednesday's 920.34 close after opening at 917.43 points.
Turnover rose to 8.18 billion drachmas from 5.78 billion on Wednesday on volume of 4.5 million shares, boosted by block trades in Parnassos, Papastratos and Ergobank.

Losers led gainers 121 to 92 with 25 issues unchanged on 238 traded. Banks fell 1.03 percent, industrials slipped 0.59 percent with construction rising 0.59 percent after plunging 4.43 percent on Monday, still trading near all time lows.
Small-caps settled higher, up 0.60 percent after tumbling 4.02 percent on Monday.

Brokers have attributed the market's recent slide to law 2396/96 which outlines the general framework governing the activities of firms offering investment services in Greece, harmonising Greek law with European Union legislation.
It has sparked selling by players forced to close out long margin positions before November 1 to comply with new regulations, they said.

On Wednesday Athens bourse president Manolis Xanthakis and capital market commission chief Stavros Thomadakis told Reuters in Boston that short selling would be allowed on the exchange before Christmas and regulated margin trading by spring 1997.

"Short selling is needed and I would like to believe that the infrastructure and regulatory framework will be there before Christmas. But to double US$ investment inflows toward Greek shares requires a quality product and more effective marketing," commented Katsabekis.
